_comment: Ship-neutral-first: every map carries IDENTITY grade values ([1,1,1], vignette 0) by default so atmosphere.gd is live end-to-end with no visible change on its own; specific maps below tune inn/street/floodplains/cave_mouth/etc for real -- see CLAUDE.md's rollout blocks. `meta.phase_thresholds` is LIVE: game.gd's `_build_sim` reads this dict and passes {dusk_at, night_at} into WIGame's `phase_config` ctor arg -- if that wiring is ever removed, WIGame._phase_config silently falls back to its own hardcoded 40/90 defaults (see wi_game.gd's phase() doc comment), so this dict genuinely drives phase timing, not just documentation. TRAP (issue #62 finding 24, the real lesson here): a PRIOR commit's comment claimed these were scaled 1.5x to 150/338 ('night arrived too fast in the first full playtest') -- but only the PROSE changed; the JSON numbers stayed 100/225 the whole time, so that fix never actually shipped and night kept arriving exactly as fast as before. Trust the live numbers, never the comment, when auditing a data file. Current values (200/450) are a genuine 2x scale off the ORIGINAL 100/225 (the 1.5x that was promised-but-never-applied, compounded with another ~1.33x on top, landing on a clean round number) -- same 2.25x dusk->night ratio preserved. Sizes the honest inn->Liscor onboarding route (measured N~60 post-Warrior-sleep actions to arrive at street; gate_district_walkthrough hits actions_since_sleep==62 at map_changed{street}) to land comfortably in DAY, dusk now well clear of that route entirely. TRAP: changing dusk/night here genuinely moves phase_changed in every event stream -- same full-canonical-seed-reverify rule as combat data (CLAUDE.md's Equipment block). atmosphere_check.json's dusk-crossing route is SIZED to dusk_at and must stay in lockstep with it; riverfarm_fight.json's night-wolf burst is sized to night_at similarly -- both re-pinned this same finding.

sewers._comment: deepened from the old cave_mouth-precedent pin (day/dusk [0.3,0.32,0.45] avg .357, night [0.26,0.28,0.4] avg .313) -- user + machine playtest concurred the sewers read too close to street-at-dusk without [Light], not like an unlit tunnel. New values sit meaningfully below the old pin while staying clearly above deep_tunnels (day/dusk [0.2,0.22,0.33] avg .25, night [0.18,0.2,0.3] avg .227) -- deep_tunnels stays the game's absolute darkest pin, the sewers escalate toward it rather than matching it. Same day/dusk/night shape as before (night a further even step down), vignette nudged 0.45->0.48 (between the old sewers pin and deep_tunnels' 0.55). Phosphor/shaft lights still glow only at dusk/night (light_energy_by_phase day=0.0); the PC's own [Light] glow (world.gd PC_LIGHT_* consts, fixed energy/radius, never phase/mood-scaled) now swings from a darker floor, so its lit-vs-unlit contrast is BIGGER, not smaller, with no change to the light itself needed. `arena_moods.sewers_nest` below is kept in lockstep (same day/dusk value) per its own "inherits the map's pin" contract -- see that entry's comment for the GH#28 legibility-boost knock-on.

guild._comment: The Adventurer's Guild interior -- "warm bureaucratic". Warmer/ambery than the inn's own grade (lamp-and-parchment read for a paperwork hall), less vignette than the street (a busy, populated room, not an oppressive one).

inn_upstairs._comment: The inn's second floor -- "warm dim". TIME-INVARIANT (same sewers/deep_tunnels precedent for a room that doesn't see the outside clock directly) rather than day/dusk/night-graded like the guild's windowed hall: a small private upstairs room reads the same at 2pm or midnight. Reuses the inn's OWN dusk grade verbatim ([0.85,0.72,0.55]) as the permanent pin -- literally 'always looks like the warm end of the day downstairs', a direct, defensible reuse rather than inventing a new palette. Same vignette as the inn (0.4) -- enclosed but not oppressive, matching a lived-in room rather than a dungeon.

barracks._comment: The Watch barracks -- "stern"/cool institutional ('barracks = stern'). Cool blue-grey, desaturated against the guild's warm amber (0.3 vignette) and the street's night-dark blue (0.44) -- reads as a spare, dutiful room rather than a welcoming or oppressive one. TIME-INVARIANT (inn_upstairs/sewers precedent): a barracks is staffed day and night, so it reads the same at any phase rather than tracking the outside clock.

runners_guild._comment: The Runner's Guild -- "brisk practical". Neutral-warm parchment/ledger tone, brighter and less saturated than the Guild's own amber (guild's [1.0,0.94,0.82]) and warmer than the barracks' cool blue-grey ([0.68,0.74,0.82]) -- a working counter-and-ledgers room, busy rather than bureaucratic or stern. TIME-INVARIANT (barracks/inn_upstairs/sewers precedent): couriers keep counter hours day and night (deliveries complete within any waking), so the room reads the same at any phase.

ruin_surface._comment: The ruin card -- "cold daylight, dusty". A SURFACE ruin sees real weather (unlike sewers/deep_tunnels' time-invariant underground pins), so it is day/dusk/night graded like inn/street/floodplains, just cooler and flatter than any of their [1,1,1]-identity day grades -- an overcast, slightly desaturated read rather than the warm/bright outdoor look. Vignette between floodplains (0.4) and sewers (0.45) -- exposed but ruined, not oppressive. The 'dusty' half of the brief is a texture/ambience call (floor tile choice + a future dust-mote emitter), not a color-grade one -- left to a later art/ambience task, ship-neutral here.

garden._comment: The only card in the game that is BOTH identity-at-every-phase AND vignette 0.0 -- every other time-invariant pin above (sewers/inn_upstairs/barracks/runners_guild) holds a DARK/desaturated triple constant across phases; this is the same mechanism (atmosphere.gd's apply() is a pure per-(map,phase) lookup, oblivious to whether the three arrays happen to be equal -- traced, not assumed, before landing this one-liner) applied to the IDENTITY grade instead. The eyes-closed test IS the mood system itself: if the screen never dims and never vignettes on this map, you are in the garden. No `arena_moods` entry, ever -- combat can never start here (the sim guard in wi_game.gd's start_combat), so an arena card would itself be a bug.

deep_tunnels._comment: The Raskghar descent -- the DARKEST pin in the game, time-invariant (below the sewers, no daylight ever reaches it). Meaningfully darker + colder than the sewers' [0.3,0.32,0.45] so the descent visibly escalates; a stronger vignette (0.55) squeezes the readable space to a lantern's reach. Any prop lights glow at every phase intent (light_energy day=0.0 still keeps day flat, so the tunnels lean on their own cold ambience).

riverfarm_village._comment: 8b R1 (issue #10). "harvest light" -- the ONLY map whose day grade tips warm (identity everywhere else is [1,1,1]); deep-blue night per spec sec.1. Values per docs/design/riverfarm-art/direction.md's Mood-card DRAFT, windowed-verified at day+dusk this task (the contrast IS the storytelling, art handoff). Issue #62 finding 22: day/dusk DEEPENED -- the old day grade (avg ~0.98, essentially full white) left the per-prop `blight_lifted` visual_states BRIGHTEN (longhouse/cottages/windmill/well tint 0.68->1.2, same warm ratio) with almost no baseline to brighten AWAY FROM -- pre-quest already read like a sunny village, so the post-quest jump barely registered. Same warm ratio preserved (R>G>B), scaled down (~0.72x day, ~0.87x dusk) so the pre-quest village reads overcast/muted -- the props' own BRIGHTEN then has real headroom to land against. Vignette nudged 0.35->0.4 (still short of the guild's 0.3<0.4<barracks' 0.36 neighbors -- a lightly oppressive, not enclosed, read) to reinforce the pre-quest mood. PROPOSED, unverified -- windowed A/B read pending (pre-quest vs. post-blight_lifted village).

witch_hollow._comment: 8b R1 (issue #10). "green shade" -- never reaches identity white even at day (canopy); dusk is the map's home key (firefly-dense per spec); vignette 0.50 > sewers' 0.45 (enclosure without an underground pin). Values per direction.md's Mood-card DRAFT.

brothers_parlor._comment: C1 FIX WAVE (controller windowed read: 'brown murk -- Wilovan a silhouette, the rug invisible'). Lifted to sit ON the shipped warm-dim legibility floor rather than below it: inn_upstairs' time-invariant [0.85,0.72,0.55]/0.4 is the codebase's own proven 'candlelit room that stays legible' pin (and the 8b night-witch fix established characters must read under the grade) -- this card lands at the same floor, one step warmer in the blue channel ([0.85,0.72,0.58]) so it stays distinct from inn_upstairs' exact grade, vignette eased 0.42->0.38. The hero-light-over-the-card-table contrast survives the lift (the table light's own energy was raised 0.9->1.0 in the same fix, mercantile decor entry). FIX ITERATION 3: vignette 0.38->0.34 alongside the floor swap (biomes.json) and Wilovan's own tint lift (skeleton_scene.json) -- the mood tint itself already sits at the inn_upstairs legibility floor and stays.

sewers_nest._comment: kept in lockstep with the deepened `moods.sewers` field pin (day/dusk [0.24,0.26,0.37], avg .29) so the vermin/nest fights still read as the SAME underground the player just walked through, not a lit-back-up combat pin. Knock-on via board_renderer.gd's GH#28 dark-arenas legibility fix (`_legibility_modulate`, self-modulates every combatant sprite/chip/HP-bar toward LEGIBILITY_TARGET 0.85): old avg .357 -> boost 0.85/.357 = 2.38x; new avg .29 -> boost 0.85/.29 = 2.93x (+23%), still under LEGIBILITY_MAX_BOOST 3.0 (not clamped) -- bat/rat enemies read brighter against the darker board with zero code change, purely a byproduct of this data-only darken. This is a read-only presentation compensation already shipped in code; this entry only supplies the mood value it reads.

deep_warren._comment: The boss arena inherits the deep_tunnels darkest pin so the Awakened Raskghar fight reads as the lowest, coldest point of the descent (matches the map grade the player crosses to reach it).
